extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduates / graduate students and researchers in mathematical thermodynamics and continuum PDEs
extracted.subtask_description: Formal/axiomatic derivation of energy, entropy, and efficiency for thermodynamic systems (homogeneous fluids, dissipative models, many-variable models, and abstract measure-theoretic systems). Presents assumptions, definitions, and theorems (First and Second Laws, existence of E and S, Clausius inequality, Carnot efficiency, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: State space Σ (homogeneous fluid model)
rubrics_metrics.description: Σ is an open, simply connected subset of (0, ∞) × (0, ∞) and its elements are called states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The simple-connectedness of Σ is used to deduce exactness of certain 1-forms (so potentials like E,S exist). Σ is a domain for temperature T>0 and volume V>0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thermodynamic constitutive regularity
rubrics_metrics.description: P, ΛV, CV are C1 (later C2 where required) functions defined on Σ. Notation P = P(T,V), ΛV = ΛV(T,V), CV = CV(T,V).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Smoothness is required to apply differential calculus (exactness of 1-forms, use of Gauss–Green, ODE existence for adiabats, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sign and monotonicity conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume ∂P/∂V < 0, ΛV ≠ 0, and CV > 0 in Σ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These physical inequalities are used repeatedly: ∂P/∂V < 0 (mechanical stability), CV>0 (thermodynamic stability), ΛV nonzero for adiabatic ODE well-posedness and Carnot picture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of paths and cycles
rubrics_metrics.description: A path Γ is an oriented, continuous, piecewise C1 curve in Σ; parameterize Γ = {(T(t),V(t)) for a ≤ t ≤ b} where T,V are C1. A cycle has matching start and end points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear distinction between geometric path and parameterized process is important later (with dissipation the parameterization matters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Work 1-form and work along a path
rubrics_metrics.description: Working 1-form defined as d−W = P dV. Work along Γ is W(Γ) = ∫_Γ P dV.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes that d−W need not be an exact differential; W(Γ) depends on the path (not only endpoints) but not on parameterization when defined as ∫ P dV.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heating 1-form and heat along a path
rubrics_metrics.description: Heating 1-form defined as d−Q = CV dT + ΛV dV. Net heat along Γ is Q(Γ) = ∫_Γ (CV dT + ΛV dV).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Again, d−Q is generally non-exact; Q(Γ) depends on path but not on parameterization in the nondissipative model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instantaneous rates of work and heat
rubrics_metrics.description: For Γ parameterized by t, rate of working w(t) = P(T(t),V(t))·V̇(t) and rate of heating q(t) = CV(T,V)·Ṫ(t) + ΛV(T,V)·V̇(t).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for converting line integrals to time integrals and for sign decomposition q = q+ - q− used in defining Q+ and Q−.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isothermal and adiabatic path definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Γ is isothermal if T(t) is constant; Γ is adiabatic if q(t) = 0 for all t.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adiabatic paths satisfy an ODE (see next criterion); isothermal pieces are used in Carnot cycles.

rubrics_metrics.name: ODE for adiabatic paths (adiabats)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adiabats can be obtained by solving dV/dT = -CV(V,T) / ΛV(V,T) for V as a function of T (parameterize V = V(T)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different initial conditions produce different adiabats; any C1 parameterization of the graph of such solutions yields an adiabatic path.

rubrics_metrics.name: First Law for cycles (nondissipative model)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume for every cycle Γ of the homogeneous fluid body, W(Γ) = Q(Γ) (conservation of energy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This axiom (together with topology of Σ) is used to deduce exactness of particular 1-forms and hence existence of an internal energy E; units must match or include mechanical equivalent of heat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence and characterization of internal energy E
rubrics_metrics.description: There exists a C2 function E(T,V) such that ∂E/∂V = ΛV − P and ∂E/∂T = CV; equivalently dE = CV dT + (ΛV − P) dV.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E is obtained because CV dT + (ΛV − P) dV is exact when ∮(CV dT + (ΛV−P) dV)=0 for every cycle; E gives Gibbs relation dE = d−Q − d−W.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carnot cycle and Carnot heat engine
rubrics_metrics.description: A Carnot cycle consists of two distinct adiabatic paths and two distinct isothermal paths. For a Carnot heat engine running between T1<T2, require Q+ > 0 (heat absorbed at T2) and Q− > 0 (heat emitted at T1); orientation indicated for positive work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carnot cycles give canonical comparison processes and lead to efficiency bounds; picture assumes ΛV>0 for the orientation drawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carnot/Second Law universality assumption
rubrics_metrics.description: Postulate that for any Carnot heat engine operating between temperatures T1<T2, W > 0 and W = (1 − T1/T2) Q+ (i.e., formula (17)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is taken as an axiom (patterned on the ideal gas calculation) that forces the universal Carnot efficiency relation and leads to the existence of entropy S.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clapeyron relation linking ΛV and P
rubrics_metrics.description: ΛV = T · (∂P/∂T) (derived by taking limiting Carnot cycles and Gauss–Green).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to verify exactness of CV/T dT + ΛV/T dV and to relate thermodynamic derivatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence and characterization of entropy S (nondissipative)
rubrics_metrics.description: There exists a C2 function S(T,V) such that ∂S/∂V = ΛV/T and ∂S/∂T = CV/T; equivalently dS = (CV/T) dT + (ΛV/T) dV and dS = d−Q/T.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows from the Carnot efficiency universality and the exactness of CV/T dT + ΛV/T dV. Yields Gibbs' formula dE = T dS − P dV.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entropy as function of (E,V) and concavity conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: S can be written as S(E,V) with ∂S/∂E = 1/T and ∂S/∂V = P/T; S is concave: ∂^2S/∂E^2 = −1/(CV T^2) < 0 and second derivatives satisfy a positive definite determinant condition (explicit formula given).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concavity of S follows from thermodynamic inequalities ∂P/∂V < 0 and CV>0 and is important for stability and variational interpretations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Efficiency definition and Carnot bound for arbitrary cycles
rubrics_metrics.description: For cycle Γ, efficiency η = W(Γ) / Q+(Γ) with 0 ≤ η ≤ 1; theorem: η ≤ 1 − T1/T2 where T1 = min_T and T2 = max_T on the cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses that ∮ dQ/T = 0 for nondissipative cycles and decomposes q into positive/negative parts to bound Q−/Q+. For Carnot cycles equality holds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissipative model constitutive form
rubrics_metrics.description: For models with dissipation: let Σ be convex open subset of (0,∞)×(0,∞); W(T,V,A,B) = P(T,V) B + R1(T,V,A,B), Q(T,V,A,B) = CV(T,V) A + ΛV(T,V) B + R2(T,V,A,B). Remainders satisfy |R1|,|R2| ≤ C (A^2 + B^2). Also same sign conditions ∂P/∂V < 0, ΛV ≠ 0, CV > 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R1,R2 capture velocity-dependent (parameterization-dependent) effects; the quadratic bound ensures these terms vanish in slow-time-scale limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process-dependent work and heat (dissipative)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a parameterized process Γ: W(Γ) = ∫_a^b W(T(t),V(t),Ṫ(t),V̇(t)) dt and Q(Γ) = ∫_a^b Q(T(t),V(t),Ṫ(t),V̇(t)) dt. In this model W(Γ), Q(Γ) depend on parameterization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrasts with nondissipative model where integrals of P dV and CV dT + ΛV dV depend only on the geometric path. Parameterization matters because of velocity-dependent remainders.

rubrics_metrics.name: First Law for dissipative model and implication for E
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume for every cyclic process Γ (parameterization included) W(Γ) = Q(Γ). From this follows existence of C2 internal energy E with ∂E/∂T = CV and ∂E/∂V = ΛV − P (same relations as nondissipative case).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proof uses time-rescaling to drive remainder terms to zero and recovers exactness of CV dT + (ΛV − P) dV.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and sign of remainder/dissipation terms
rubrics_metrics.description: From the cyclic First Law and reparameterization argument one deduces R1 ≡ R2, and it is reasonable to assume R1 = R2 ≤ 0 for all arguments (representing lost work due to internal friction/dissipation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpreting R1=R2 ≤ 0 gives a physical meaning: negative remainder reduces available work; it leads to strict Clausius inequalities for irreversible processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clausius inequality for dissipative model
rubrics_metrics.description: For any cyclic process Γ, ∮_Γ (d−Q / T) ≤ 0. More generally for a process Γ from α to β, ∫_Γ (d−Q / T) ≤ S(β) − S(α).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inequality follows from R1=R2 ≤ 0 and dS = d−Q/T for the nondissipative part; becomes equality for reversible processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Efficiency bound persists with dissipation
rubrics_metrics.description: For a cyclic process with maximum temperature T2 and minimum T1, efficiency satisfies η ≤ 1 − T1/T2 even in the dissipative model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof similar to nondissipative case but uses Clausius inequality ∮ dQ/T ≤ 0 instead of equality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Many-variable (Day–Silhavý) model: state space and generalized latents
rubrics_metrics.description: State space Σ ⊂ R^n open simply connected; T: Σ → (0,∞) and Λ = (Λ1,...,Λn) : Σ → R^n are C2 (temperature and generalized latent heats). Paths, cycles, Q(Γ)=∫_Γ Λ·dY, and decompositions q = q+ − q− are defined analogously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This generalizes the two-variable T,V picture to n variables, carrying over notions of adiabatic, isothermal, absorbing/emitting and Carnot paths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main Hypothesis for many-variable model (existence of monotone isotherms)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each pair of states α,β ∈ Σ and for each temperature level θ attained in Σ, there exists a monotone, essentially isothermal path Γ ∈ M(α,β) such that T(Y(t)) = θ on the heating/emitting portions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This technical hypothesis is used in constructing a consistent entropy function from inequality constraints (enables concatenation arguments and additivity properties).

rubrics_metrics.name: Efficiency inequalities implying entropy existence (many-variable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume (2) for each cycle: ξ(Γ) ≤ 0 where ξ is crude entropy change, and (3) for Carnot cycles equality holds; equivalently W(Γ) ≤ (1 − T−(Γ)/T+(Γ)) Q+(Γ) for cycles and equality for Carnot cycles. Then there exists C2 function S with ∂S/∂Y_k = Λ_k/T.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These efficiency-type estimates are both necessary and sufficient (conversely S implies these inequalities). The proof constructs a function φ bounding ξ and uses additivity to define S.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crude entropy ξ(Γ) and its cycle/Carnot properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Define ξ(Γ) = 0 if Γ is adiabatic, otherwise ξ(Γ) = Q+(Γ)/T+(Γ) − Q−(Γ)/T−(Γ). Then cycles satisfy ξ(Γ) ≤ 0 and Carnot cycles satisfy ξ(Γ) = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ξ is used as an intermediate construct to compare different processes and deduce existence and additivity properties ultimately yielding S.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract thermodynamic system axioms (Feinberg–Lavine)
rubrics_metrics.description: Σ is a compact metric space; processes P ⊂ M0(Σ) × M(Σ) form a closed convex cone. For Γ = (ν,µ): ν ∈ M0(Σ) is change of condition, µ ∈ M(Σ) is heating measure. Cyclic processes are those with ν = 0 and their heating measures form C = {µ | (0,µ)∈P}. Postulate Second Law as C ∩ M+(Σ) = {0}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract, measure-theoretic formalism models bodies with distributions of microstates and general processes; the Second Law forbids purely nonnegative heating measures for cycles (no perfect conversion of heat to work).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hahn–Banach separation to produce S and T
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the above abstract hypotheses, separate the cone of processes K1 = P and K2 = {0} × M1+(Σ) to obtain a continuous linear functional Φ(ν,µ) = ∫ ψ dν + ∫ φ dµ with φ > 0. Define S := −ψ and T := 1/φ yielding the inequality ∫ dµ/T ≤ ∫ S dν for each process (26).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a functional-analytic derivation of entropy and temperature: the separating hyperplane yields continuous S and strictly positive T, giving Clausius-type inequalities and characterizing reversible processes by equality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clausius inequality and reversibility in abstract model
rubrics_metrics.description: Define Γ ↦ ∫ dµ/T as ∫_Γ d−Q/T; then for cyclic processes ∫_Γ d−Q/T ≤ 0 and for processes from α to β, ∫_Γ d−Q/T ≤ S(β) − S(α). Reversible processes satisfy equality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This repackages the abstract inequality (26) into the familiar Clausius form and shows that equality characterizes reversible processes.
